headings: Rules by the Lord of the seventh house.
Whether the Thiefe be in the Towne or no.
Distance betwixt the Owner and the Thief.
Toward what part the Thief is gone.
Which way the Thief is gone.

units.section_heading: Rules by the Lord of the seventh house.
units.short_original_anchor: Rules by the Lord of the seventh house.
units.normalized_historical_statement: Printed p343 introduces rules organized by the house occupied by the lord of the seventh. These are the author's historical conjectures concerning a supposed taker and lost goods.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The nearby handwritten number is not part of the printed heading.

units.section_heading: Rules by the Lord of the seventh house.
units.short_original_anchor: The Lord of the seventh in the ascendant or fourth
units.normalized_historical_statement: On printed p343, the author assigns the seventh lord in the ascendant or fourth to someone of the house or household, or someone frequenting the house; he places this person in the city or town, among those the querent least mistrusts, and predicts that the person will hardly confess the alleged act.
preconditions: Lord of the seventh in the ascendant OR fourth house.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The fourth house receives a further, distinct set of alternatives later on the same page.

units.section_heading: Rules by the Lord of the seventh house.
units.short_original_anchor: one of the houshold,or an acquaintance
units.normalized_historical_statement: On printed p343, with the seventh lord in the second and in a masculine sign, the author conjectures someone of the household or an acquaintance.
preconditions: Lord of the seventh in the second house.
The sign is masculine.

units.section_heading: Rules by the Lord of the seventh house.
units.short_original_anchor: if it be in a feminine Signe, it is his Wife
units.normalized_historical_statement: On printed p343, the feminine-sign alternative for the seventh lord in the second is conjecturally the wife, perhaps a sweetheart or maid of the house.
preconditions: Lord of the seventh in the second house.
The sign is feminine.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The author expressly qualifies the sweetheart or maid alternative with 'perhaps'.

units.section_heading: Rules by the Lord of the seventh house.
units.short_original_anchor: and may be recovered by money.
units.normalized_historical_statement: On printed p343, the second-house paragraph additionally places the subject within the loser's power or among those of his house and claims recovery may be obtained by money.
preconditions: Lord of the seventh in the second house.
Read with the masculine and feminine alternatives immediately preceding it.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The sentence shifts between the supposed person and recovery without explicitly restating the object of 'recovered'; that grammatical ambiguity is retained.

units.section_heading: Rules by the Lord of the seventh house.
units.short_original_anchor: The Lord of the seventh in the third
units.normalized_historical_statement: On printed p343, the seventh lord in the third is assigned conjecturally to kindred, a brother, sisters, cousins, 'his onely Fellow by way of service', a neighbour often in his sight, or his disciple, messenger or servant, with an open-ended '&c.'
preconditions: Lord of the seventh in the third house.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The printed alternatives are not an exhaustive list; the paragraph ends '&c.'.

units.section_heading: Rules by the Lord of the seventh house.
units.short_original_anchor: The Lord of the seventh in the fourth
units.normalized_historical_statement: On printed p343, the separate fourth-house paragraph conjectures the father, an old person, someone of the father's kin, or someone dwelling in the father's heritage or house. It additionally supposes that the taker has given the thing to his wife, or a woman to her husband; alternatively it names the goodman or goodwife of the house, or a tiller or the labour role indicated by the printed 'Labou-' of the land for the querent.
preconditions: Lord of the seventh in the fourth house.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: These alternatives supplement, rather than replace, the earlier ascendant-or-fourth rule.
The labour word appears incomplete at the line break; its missing completion is not supplied.

units.section_heading: Rules by the Lord of the seventh house.
units.short_original_anchor: the Sonne or Daughter of him
units.normalized_historical_statement: On printed p343, the seventh lord in the fifth is assigned conjecturally to his son or daughter, or the son or daughter of his cousin or nephew, followed by the parenthetical masculine-sign condition; the paragraph also offers someone of his father's household or his very friend.
preconditions: Lord of the seventh in the fifth house.
The printed parenthesis says '(if the Sign be a masculine)'.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The parenthesis follows the child-of-cousin-or-nephew alternatives; its exact reach across the preceding alternatives is not made explicit.
The source's pronouns are retained without inventing named relationships.

units.section_heading: Rules by the Lord of the seventh house.
units.short_original_anchor: a Servant, a Disciple or Labourer to the querent
units.normalized_historical_statement: On printed p343, the seventh lord in the sixth is conjecturally a servant, disciple or labourer to the querent; someone conversant with a churchman; a brother or sister of the father; or someone the author describes as sick, unsteadfast or grieved.
preconditions: Lord of the seventh in the sixth house.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The bodily and personal descriptions are the author's conjectures, not clinical findings or identification evidence.

units.section_heading: Rules by the Lord of the seventh house.
units.short_original_anchor: his Wife or Lady, or an Harlot
units.normalized_historical_statement: On printed p343, the seventh lord in the seventh is conjecturally the wife or lady, a person the source calls a harlot, a woman customarily suspected in such matters, or a buyer or seller in markets.
preconditions: Lord of the seventh in the seventh house.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: These descriptions record the author's allegations and social categories.
The following feminine-sign clause is preserved separately rather than silently attached to all these alternatives.

units.section_heading: Rules by the Lord of the seventh house.
units.short_original_anchor: if it be a feminine Signe
units.normalized_historical_statement: On printed p343, after the seventh-house alternatives, the explicit feminine-sign clause says that the taker is an utter enemy of the loser because of a former cause between them, dwells somewhat far from him, still has the things in custody, and that recovery is hard.
preconditions: Lord of the seventh in the seventh house.
The subsequent clause explicitly begins 'if it be a feminine Signe'.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The feminine-sign condition occurs after the market buyer-or-seller alternative and before the enemy statement.
The margin warns that this passage must be understood warily.

units.section_heading: Rules by the Lord of the seventh house.
units.short_original_anchor: This must be warily understood.
units.normalized_historical_statement: The printed p343 margin cautions that the adjoining seventh-house passage must be understood warily.
preconditions: Marginal qualification beside the seventh-house paragraph.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The author supplies no further explanation of the caution here.

units.section_heading: Rules by the Lord of the seventh house.
units.short_original_anchor: The Lord of the seventh in the eighth,a Stranger
units.normalized_historical_statement: Across printed pp343–344, the eighth-house conjecture begins with a stranger who nevertheless seems to be of the household, an open enemy, a near kinswoman because of some offence, or an evilly disposed person 'of the Livery of the Man'. The author says this person comes to his house and is either maintained by him or performs servile acts, such as a butcher or labourer sometimes killing cattle. He says the lost thing seems recoverable only through fair words, dread of death or threats. Alternatively, the thing is lost by an absent man who is not presently remembered and seems quite forgotten.
preconditions: Lord of the seventh in the eighth house.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The author uses 'yet seemeth' and 'it seemeth', preserving conjectural modality.
The stranger is not converted into a definitive household identification.
The final absent-man alternative is retained separately within the statement.
The page break divides 'seemeth' between printed pp343 and 344.

units.section_heading: Rules by the Lord of the seventh house.
units.short_original_anchor: The Lord of the seventh in the ninth
units.normalized_historical_statement: On printed p344, the seventh lord in the ninth is conjecturally an honest person, clerk or churchman; the author places the supposed thief out of the way or country and alternatively describes a disciple, governor to a master of a privileged place, or poor vagrant. He says recovery is hard except through a religious person as previously stated.
preconditions: Lord of the seventh in the ninth house.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The exception is recovery through a religious person.
The backward reference 'as aforesaid' is retained without supplying material outside this window.
The source does not explicitly restate what is to be recovered.

units.section_heading: Rules by the Lord of the seventh house.
units.short_original_anchor: if the Figure be Feminine, & e contra
units.normalized_historical_statement: On printed p344, the seventh lord in the tenth is conjecturally a lord, master or governor in the king's house or household, a lady or gentlewoman if the figure is feminine, with '& e contra', or a crafts-master. The author adds that it is usually someone living handsomely who is not necessitated to this course of life.
preconditions: Lord of the seventh in the tenth house.
The lady-or-gentlewoman alternative expressly depends on the figure being feminine.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The source says 'Figure', not specifically 'Signe', in this condition.
The reciprocal '& e contra' is retained without inventing a more detailed rule.
The final description is qualified by 'usually'.

units.section_heading: Rules by the Lord of the seventh house.
units.short_original_anchor: I ever finde it to signifie one
units.normalized_historical_statement: In the printed p344 margin beside the tenth-house paragraph, the author says he invariably finds it to signify someone lodging in the house when the thing was lost, or using the house.
preconditions: Marginal first-person observation adjoining the seventh-lord-in-the-tenth rule.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: This is an asserted author observation, not a presented worked case or chart.

units.section_heading: Rules by the Lord of the seventh house.
units.short_original_anchor: The Lord of the seventh in the eleventh
units.normalized_historical_statement: On printed p344, the seventh lord in the eleventh is conjecturally a friend, someone known through a service done, someone of a churchman's or neighbour's household, or a servant where the querent has some lordship who is put in trust; another alternative is someone of the household of the querent's mother. The author claims recovery can occur again through such a person's means.
preconditions: Lord of the seventh in the eleventh house.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The printed wording around the querent and his mother is awkward; the maternal-household alternative is retained without assigning additional relationships.

units.section_heading: Rules by the Lord of the seventh house.
units.short_original_anchor: a false person, and inthralled, incumbred or oppressed with poverty
units.normalized_historical_statement: On printed p344, the seventh lord in the twelfth is conjecturally a stranger, envious and false, enthralled, encumbered or oppressed by poverty, and without riches. The author consequently supposes that the person has visited many regions as an enemy or beggar and rejoices in it.
preconditions: Lord of the seventh in the twelfth house.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: These personal, moral and economic descriptions are historical author conjectures rather than findings about a person.

units.section_heading: Rules by the Lord of the seventh house.
units.short_original_anchor: judge his quality by the Signe and Place
units.normalized_historical_statement: On printed p344, the author directs the reader to judge the supposed person's quality by sign and place and to combine all the preceding house rules with other testimonies of signs and planets.
preconditions: Application of the preceding seventh-lord house rules.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The house rules are expressly to be combined with other testimonies rather than treated as sufficient alone.

units.section_heading: Whether the Thiefe be in the Towne or no.
units.short_original_anchor: Whether the Thiefe be in the Towne or no.
units.normalized_historical_statement: Printed p344 opens a subsection concerning whether the supposed thief remains in the town.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The adjacent handwritten number is excluded from the printed heading.

units.section_heading: Whether the Thiefe be in the Towne or no.
units.short_original_anchor: in the end of a Signe direct
units.normalized_historical_statement: Across printed pp344–345, the author says to pronounce the supposed thief gone or going out of town if the thief's significator is at the end of a sign and direct, or is separating from combustion, or is applying to a planet in the third or ninth house.
preconditions: Thief's significator at the end of a sign AND direct; OR
Thief's significator separating FROM combustion; OR
Thief's significator applying TO a planet situated in the third OR ninth house.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The alternatives are retained as printed.
No particular aspect glyph is specified for the application.
Printed p344 ends 'gon'; p345 continues 'or going out of the Town'.

units.section_heading: Whether the Thiefe be in the Towne or no.
units.short_original_anchor: out of one Signe into another,denoteth change of Lodging
units.normalized_historical_statement: On printed p345, the author explains that the significator's movement from one sign into another denotes a change of lodging or removal.
preconditions: The relevant significator moves out of one sign into another.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: This is the author's stated rationale adjoining the departure rule, not an independently verified movement.

units.section_heading: Whether the Thiefe be in the Towne or no.
units.short_original_anchor: if it be a superiour Planet, the rule is infallible.
units.normalized_historical_statement: On printed p345, the author claims the preceding rule is infallible if the significator is a superior planet.
preconditions: The significator in the preceding departure/change-of-sign discussion is a superior planet.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The author asserts infallibility; the outline does not endorse it.
The planets included in 'superiour' are not enumerated here.

units.section_heading: Whether the Thiefe be in the Towne or no.
units.short_original_anchor: but above ninety degrees asunder
units.normalized_historical_statement: On printed p345, if the ascendant lord and the Moon are not in one quarter and are more than ninety degrees apart, the author infers departure or a great distance between the goods and their owner.
preconditions: Ascendant lord and Moon are not in the same quarter.
They are above ninety degrees apart.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The stated distance is between goods and owner, not expressly between thief and owner.

units.section_heading: Whether the Thiefe be in the Towne or no.
units.short_original_anchor: and applying to Planets in angles
units.normalized_historical_statement: On printed p345, if the ascendant lord and Moon are in angles and applying to planets in angles, the author infers no far distance, especially when the Moon and ascendant lord are in the same quarter.
preconditions: Ascendant lord and Moon are in angles.
They apply TO planets that are also in angles.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The same-quarter condition strengthens the claim through 'especially'.
The author specifies no particular application aspect here.
This opposing distance judgment is preserved separately from the more-than-ninety-degrees rule.

units.section_heading: Distance betwixt the Owner and the Thief.
units.short_original_anchor: Distance betwixt the Owner and the Thief.
units.normalized_historical_statement: Printed p345 introduces a subsection assigning distance between owner and supposed thief.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Handwritten numerals beside the heading are not printed conditions.

units.section_heading: Distance betwixt the Owner and the Thief.
units.short_original_anchor: If the Thief, viz. his Significator, be in a fixed Signe
units.normalized_historical_statement: On printed p345, the author gives a method based on the thief's significator's sign: in a fixed sign, count three miles for every house between the ascendant lord and that significator; in common signs, count one mile for every house between the ascendant and thief; in movable signs, count as many terrestrial houses between loser and thief as there are houses between the ascendant and thief.
preconditions: Fixed-sign branch: thief's significator in a fixed sign; count houses between ASCENDANT LORD and thief's significator.
Common-sign branch: thief's significator in a common sign; the printed endpoints are ASCENDANT and thief.
Movable-sign branch: thief's significator in a movable sign; the printed endpoints are ASCENDANT and thief.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The fixed branch names the lord of the ascendant; the other branches name the ascendant. That difference is not silently corrected.
The movable branch counts physical houses, rather than miles.
A margin qualifies these judgments by reference to the country.

units.section_heading: Distance betwixt the Owner and the Thief.
units.short_original_anchor: If the Signe ascending be a fixed Signe
units.normalized_historical_statement: On printed p345, the author gives another distance scale based on the ascending sign: three miles for every house when fixed, one mile when common, and half a mile when movable.
preconditions: Use the ASCENDING SIGN for this method.
Fixed ascending sign: three miles per house.
Common ascending sign: one mile per house.
Movable ascending sign: half a mile per house.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: This paragraph does not independently restate the endpoints of the house count.
This ascending-sign method is preserved separately from the thief-significator method, whose movable branch uses physical houses.

units.section_heading: Distance betwixt the Owner and the Thief.
units.short_original_anchor: These judgments best agree from the Country.
units.normalized_historical_statement: The printed p345 margin qualifies the distance judgments with the wording that they 'best agree from the Country'.
preconditions: Marginal qualification beside the distance scales.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The unusual preposition 'from' is retained rather than rewritten into a more definite geographical restriction.

units.section_heading: Distance betwixt the Owner and the Thief.
units.short_original_anchor: he is still in the Towne
units.normalized_historical_statement: On printed p345, the thief's significator in an angle is said to mean the supposed thief is still in town; in a succedent, not far off; in cadents, far gone.
preconditions: Classify the thief's significator as angular, succedent or cadent.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: This qualitative placement method remains distinct from the preceding numerical distance scales.

units.section_heading: Where the Thief is.
units.short_original_anchor: Where the Thief is.
units.normalized_historical_statement: Printed p345 introduces a subsection concerning the supposed thief's location.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The heading itself contains only four words.

units.section_heading: Where the Thief is.
units.short_original_anchor: In an angle, at home
units.normalized_historical_statement: On printed p345, the Moon in an angle is said to indicate home; in a succedent, about home; in a cadent, far from home.
preconditions: The paragraph begins with the printed Moon crescent glyph.
Classify the Moon's placement as angular, succedent or cadent.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The subject is the Moon, not the thief's significator used in the preceding subsection.

units.section_heading: Where the Thief is.
units.short_original_anchor: These are fitt for the Country.
units.normalized_historical_statement: The printed p345 margin says the adjoining location judgments are fit for the country.
preconditions: Marginal qualification adjoining the location rules.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The note is retained without extending it into a universal restriction on later sections.

units.section_heading: Where the Thief is.
units.short_original_anchor: The Significator of the Thief in an angle
units.normalized_historical_statement: On printed p345, the thief's significator in an angle is said to place the supposed thief in a house.
preconditions: Thief's significator in an angle.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: This rule says a house; the following Moon rule adds ownership.

units.section_heading: Where the Thief is.
units.short_original_anchor: in his owne house
units.normalized_historical_statement: On printed p345, the Moon in an angle is said to place the supposed thief in his own house.
preconditions: Moon in an angle, as shown by the printed crescent glyph.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The possessive qualification belongs to this Moon branch.

units.section_heading: Where the Thief is.
units.short_original_anchor: in a succedant, he is in Closes
units.normalized_historical_statement: On printed p345, the thief's significator in a succedent is said to place the supposed thief in closes.
preconditions: Thief's significator in a succedent house.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The following Moon branch supplies the separate 'his owne' qualification.

units.section_heading: Where the Thief is.
units.short_original_anchor: in a succedant, in his owne Closes.
units.normalized_historical_statement: On printed p345, the Moon in a succedent is said to place the supposed thief in his own closes.
preconditions: Moon in a succedent house, as indicated by the printed crescent glyph.

units.section_heading: Where the Thief is.
units.short_original_anchor: The Significator of the Thief in a cadent house
units.normalized_historical_statement: On printed p345, the thief's significator in a cadent house is said to place the supposed thief in a common.
preconditions: Thief's significator in a cadent house.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The source's land category 'Common' is retained.

units.section_heading: Where the Thief is.
units.short_original_anchor: in his owne Common, or that which belongs to the Towne
units.normalized_historical_statement: On printed p345, the Moon in a cadent is said to place the supposed thief in his own common or the common belonging to the town where he lives.
preconditions: Moon in a cadent house, as indicated by the printed crescent glyph.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Both the own-common and town-common alternatives are retained.

units.section_heading: Where the Thief is.
units.short_original_anchor: within thirty degrees of the Lord of the ascendant
units.normalized_historical_statement: Across printed pp345–346, the author says the thief is near the person who lost the goods when the thief's significator is within thirty degrees of the ascendant lord; within seventy degrees, the thief is within that person's town or parish. He adds that more degrees between them mean they are farther apart.
preconditions: Measure degrees between the thief's significator and the ascendant lord.
Within thirty degrees: near the loser.
Within seventy degrees: within the loser's town or parish.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The author does not specify an application or separation direction here.
The seventy-degree statement is not rewritten as an exclusive thirty-to-seventy-degree interval.
The sentence crosses the page break after 'lost the' and resumes with 'Goods'.

units.section_heading: Where the Thief is.
units.short_original_anchor: he is out of the Towne
units.normalized_historical_statement: On printed p346, the thief's significator in a square aspect to the ascendant lord is said to indicate that the supposed thief is out of town.
preconditions: Thief's significator in the printed square aspect, represented by a square glyph, TO the ascendant lord.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The source does not specify whether this square is applying or separating.

units.section_heading: Where the Thief is.
units.short_original_anchor: the Thief is not yet gone out of the Town
units.normalized_historical_statement: On printed p346, a strong seventh lord in an angle is said to mean that the supposed thief has not yet left the town or parish where the alleged theft occurred.
preconditions: Lord of the seventh is strong.
Lord of the seventh is in an angle.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The source does not define strength in this paragraph.

units.section_heading: Where the Thief is.
units.short_original_anchor: he is gone, or departing.
units.normalized_historical_statement: On printed p346, the contrasting branch says that if the seventh lord is found weak in an angle, the supposed thief is gone or departing.
preconditions: Lord of the seventh is weak.
Lord of the seventh is in an angle.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Both 'gone' and 'departing' remain alternatives.
This opposing strength-dependent branch is preserved separately from the strong-angular rule.

units.section_heading: Another.
units.short_original_anchor: Another.
units.normalized_historical_statement: Printed p346 introduces another group of location rules under the unnumbered printed heading 'Another.'.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The printed heading contains one word; the adjacent handwritten number is excluded.

units.section_heading: Another.
units.short_original_anchor: the Thiefe will be at home (before him)
units.normalized_historical_statement: On printed p346, if the seventh lord is in the ascendant, the author instructs the reader to tell the querent that the supposed thief will be at home before him, or before he gets home, and appends 'probatum est'.
preconditions: Lord of the seventh in the ascendant.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The claim of proof is the author's.
The adjoining margin qualifies this assertion with 'sometimes'.

units.section_heading: Another.
units.short_original_anchor: the Thiefe brings the Goods home willingly.
units.normalized_historical_statement: In the printed p346 margin, the author says it sometimes holds true that the seventh lord in the ascendant signifies the supposed thief bringing the goods home willingly.
preconditions: Lord of the seventh in the ascendant.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The author expressly says 'It sometimes holds true'.
Willing return of the goods is an additional marginal claim, not merely arrival home before the querent.

units.section_heading: Another.
units.short_original_anchor: he is hid at home and dare not be seen.
units.normalized_historical_statement: On printed p346, the seventh lord in the seventh is said to mean that the supposed thief is hidden at home and dares not be seen.
preconditions: Lord of the seventh in the seventh house.

units.section_heading: Another.
units.short_original_anchor: If the Lord of the sixt be in the first or second
units.normalized_historical_statement: On printed p346, the author conjectures that the supposed thief is of the querent's house if the sixth lord is in the first or second, with an additional clause involving any of their lords.
preconditions: Lord of the sixth in the first OR second house.
The following printed clause involves 'any of their Lords'; its connective is uncertain in the image.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The connective resembles 'will' or 'with'; a definite conjunction or application condition is not supplied.
No aspect glyph is stated.

units.section_heading: Another.
units.short_original_anchor: the Thief is with the Querent
units.normalized_historical_statement: On printed p346, when the ascendant lord and thief's significator are together, the author says the supposed thief is with the querent, appends 'probatum est', calls it the very truth and says the person cannot be far from him.
preconditions: Ascendant lord and thief's significator are 'together'.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The source does not print a conjunction glyph or specify an orb here.
The assertions of proof and truth are the author's.

units.section_heading: Toward what part the Thief is gone.
units.short_original_anchor: Toward what part the Thief is gone.
units.normalized_historical_statement: Printed p346 introduces the direction supposedly taken after departure from town.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The adjacent handwritten number is not part of the printed heading.

units.section_heading: Toward what part the Thief is gone.
units.short_original_anchor: behold the Planet that signifies his going out of Towne
units.normalized_historical_statement: On printed p346, to conjecture where the supposed thief fled after leaving town, the author directs the reader to the planet signifying that departure and its sign: fiery means the east part of town or country; watery, north; airy, west; earthly, south.
preconditions: The inquiry concerns flight after going out of town.
Use the planet signifying the going out of town.
Fiery sign: east.
Watery sign: north.
Airy sign: west.
Earthly sign: south.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The departure-signifying planet is not explicitly equated here with every other significator used in subsequent methods.

units.section_heading: Toward what part the Thief is gone.
units.short_original_anchor: preferring the Sign before the quarter
units.normalized_historical_statement: On printed p346, the author also directs judgment by the planet's quarter of heaven: a signifier in the west means west, and he describes the east part as extending from the midheaven to the ascendant, followed by '&c.'. He says to combine sign and quarter, prefer the sign, and use the quarter only to balance judgment when other testimonies are equal.
preconditions: Consider the relevant planet's quarter of heaven as well as its sign.
West placement: west.
The printed east-sector example runs from midheaven to ascendant.
Use the quarter to balance the judgment when OTHER TESTIMONIES ARE EQUAL.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The sign expressly has priority over the quarter.
The source's '&c.' is not expanded into an unprinted full quadrant table.

units.section_heading: Toward what part the Thief is gone.
units.short_original_anchor: be more fully explicated in the succeeding sheet.
units.normalized_historical_statement: The printed p346 margin says these matters will be explained more fully in the succeeding sheet.
preconditions: Marginal forward reference beside the directional discussion.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The reference is recorded without importing explanations beyond the requested stopping boundary.

units.section_heading: Which way the Thief is gone.
units.short_original_anchor: Which way the Thief is gone.
units.normalized_historical_statement: Printed p347 opens a further subsection presenting several methods for conjecturing the direction taken by the supposed thief.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The heading is printed; its adjoining number is handwritten.

units.section_heading: Which way the Thief is gone.
units.short_original_anchor: Behold the significant Planet, in what Signe he is
units.normalized_historical_statement: On printed p347, the first method judges direction from the significant planet's sign and also its quarter.
preconditions: Identify the significant planet.
Inspect both its sign and quarter.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The subsection immediately reports other methods, which are preserved separately.

units.section_heading: Which way the Thief is gone.
units.short_original_anchor: others judge by the place
units.normalized_historical_statement: On printed p347, the author reports that others judge the supposed thief's direction by the Moon's place.
preconditions: Alternative method attributed to 'others'.
Use the place of the Moon, shown by the printed crescent glyph.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: This is not merged into the significant-planet method.

units.section_heading: Which way the Thief is gone.
units.short_original_anchor: the Lord of the seventh, and the Lord of the hour
units.normalized_historical_statement: On printed p347, another reported method considers the seventh lord and hour lord, their signs and quarters, and judges by those indications if they agree.
preconditions: Use BOTH the lord of the seventh and the lord of the hour.
Inspect the signs and quarters they occupy.
Proceed by their indications IF THEY AGREE.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The author supplies no rule here for disagreement between them.

units.section_heading: Which way the Thief is gone.
units.short_original_anchor: to whom he doth apply, or render his power
units.normalized_historical_statement: On printed p347, the author reports that others regard the significator to whom the relevant planet applies or renders its power when judging direction.
preconditions: Identify the significator TO WHOM the relevant planet applies OR renders its power.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The application recipient is the object of this method; the direction of application is not reversed.
The pronoun 'he' is not more precisely resolved in this clause.
No particular aspect or definition of rendering power is supplied.

units.section_heading: Which way the Thief is gone.
units.short_original_anchor: others by the Lord of the fourth
units.normalized_historical_statement: On printed p347, the author reports another directional method using the lord of the fourth.
preconditions: Use the lord of the fourth for this reported alternative method.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The source does not elaborate this method here.

units.section_heading: Which way the Thief is gone.
units.short_original_anchor: I alwayes judge by the strongest
units.normalized_historical_statement: On printed p347, the author's own stated practice is always to judge by whichever is strongest, the significator or the Moon.
preconditions: Compare the strength of the significator and Moon.
Use the stronger of these two.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The author distinguishes his own practice from the preceding methods attributed to others.
No strength calculation or tie-breaking rule is printed here.

units.section_heading: Which way the Thief is gone.
units.short_original_anchor: If the Significator of the Thief be in a fiery Sign
units.normalized_historical_statement: On printed p347, the author repeats a directional mapping expressly for the thief's significator: fiery sign means the supposed thief went east; earthly, south; airy, west; watery, north.
preconditions: Use the THIEF'S SIGNIFICATOR for this rule.
Fiery sign: east.
Earthly sign: south.
Airy sign: west.
Watery sign: north.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: This repetition is retained because the named subject differs from the departure-signifying planet on printed p346.

units.section_heading: Which way the Thief is gone.
units.short_original_anchor: there is the Thief
units.normalized_historical_statement: On printed p347, the author says to see which angle contains the Moon and places the supposed thief there.
preconditions: Moon is in an angle.
Use the angle occupied by the Moon.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The subject is supplied by the printed Moon crescent glyph.

units.section_heading: Which way the Thief is gone.
units.short_original_anchor: in no angle look for the Lord of the house
units.normalized_historical_statement: On printed p347, if the Moon is in no angle, the author instead directs attention to the lord of the Moon's house and says the supposed thief went to that part.
preconditions: Moon is in NO angle.
Look for the lord of the house of the Moon.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The text does not independently explain how to determine that lord's directional part here.
The phrase 'house of the Moon' is retained without replacing it with a guessed cusp or a more specific technical definition.

units.section_heading: Which way the Thief is gone.
units.short_original_anchor: See what Signe the Lord of the seventh is in
units.normalized_historical_statement: On printed p347, the author gives a sign-specific directional method for the seventh lord: in the printed Aries glyph, eastward; in the printed Taurus glyph, 'in the South against the east'; he then says 'and so of the rest'.
preconditions: Inspect the SIGN of the lord of the seventh.
Aries glyph: eastward.
Taurus glyph: south against the east.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The glyphs are recognizable as Aries and Taurus; their names are normalized readings rather than words printed in this sentence.
The source's wording 'South against the east' is retained rather than silently converted into a precise bearing.
'And so of the rest' is not expanded into unprinted sign assignments.

units.section_heading: Which way the Thief is gone.
units.short_original_anchor: The peculiar quarter of heaven every Signe naturally signifies doth follow hereafter.
units.normalized_historical_statement: The printed p347 margin says that the particular quarter of heaven naturally signified by each sign follows hereafter.
preconditions: Marginal forward reference adjoining the directional rules.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: No later sign-direction table is supplied or reconstructed in this window.
